purpose: SPEC-04 §2 addendum (2026-09-26) coverage + A1 conditions C8/C9/C10, FIX ROUND 3: a blocking gap in round 2's /blog fix (compareEntry never diffed embeddedPostsError when both sides had the SAME error — the listing could silently drop out of parity) plus 4 robustness notes.

fixRound3.note: Round 2 (fixRound2 below, git sha 4f532b0) was reviewed a third time before being committed; that review (recorded by the orchestrator as ae99b2d, LOG.md/STATE.json only — no code was committed) found one BLOCKING issue in the /blog change plus 4 robustness notes. All fixed and re-verified live below.

blocking.gap: compareEntry() only pushed an embeddedPostsError diff when a.embeddedPostsError !== b.embeddedPostsError. If BOTH sides failed /blog extraction with the SAME error message (e.g. the same Next.js version on both, hitting the same parser edge case), no diff was recorded at all and the reviewer confirmed failedUnallowed stayed 0 — the entire /blog listing would silently drop out of parity exactly when the harness itself was most likely to be blind (a shared extraction failure).
fix: compare.mjs: the embeddedPostsError check now pushes a diff whenever EITHER side has an error, unconditionally (not gated on inequality). 'embeddedPostsError' is now in FORBIDDEN_ALLOWLIST_FIELDS (alongside the new 'embeddedPostsMissing'), so it can never be allowlisted away either — verified live: a synthetic same-error-both-sides manifest pair now produces failedUnallowed=1.

compare.mjs: new checkEmbeddedPostsCoverage(manifestA, manifestB) — a 2xx /blog(-like) entry with NEITHER embeddedPosts* fields NOR embeddedPostsError (the capture code never even attempted extraction) now fails as field 'embeddedPostsMissing'. Gated on a NEW manifest-level marker (capture.mjs's capture() now returns `harness: {embeddedPosts: 1}`) so an OLDER manifest captured before this feature existed is never wrongly judged by a rule it couldn't have satisfied — verified live with 3 synthetic cases: same-error-both-sides fails; a new-code (marker present) bare 2xx /blog entry on both sides fails; the identical bare entry on an OLD manifest (no marker) does NOT fail.
blocking.selfTestCasesAdded: 'embedded-posts-coverage-guard': both sides with the same embeddedPostsError must fail (verified); a new-code 2xx /blog entry with neither fields nor error must fail (verified); the same case on an old (unmarked) manifest must NOT fail (verified) — all 3 passed live.

nonBlockingFixed: lib/extract.mjs's RSC flight parser rewritten to JOIN all self.__next_f.push() strings in document order FIRST, then split the joined buffer into rows (id:data, newline-terminated, except 'T' text rows which use an explicit hex BYTE-length prefix and can contain literal newlines in their own payload) — instead of treating each push() call as exactly one row, which silently skipped 6 of 13 live push() calls that actually held several rows each. Also found and fixed a real edge case while verifying: some rows have an EMPTY id (a bare ':HL[...]' hint row) — my first cut's row-id regex required at least one hex digit and stopped parsing dead at the first one, undercounting rows 42 vs the reviewer's 49; fixed with an optional hex-digit id. Verified live: the join-then-split parser now finds exactly 49 rows, consumes the ENTIRE joined buffer (byte-exact), and finds exactly one 172-post array — matching the reviewer's own test exactly. extractEmbeddedBlogPosts() now also requires EXACTLY ONE candidate array (throws on >1, not 'keep the longest'), matching its own docstring.

New self-test 'flight-row-batching-robustness': using the REAL 172-post row recovered from a live /blog capture, (1) merged into one push() call alongside other non-JSON rows before and after it, and (2) split mid-JSON across two separate push() calls — both still extract all 172 posts in the same order. Both passed live.

functional/run.mjs: fetchWithTimeout() now wraps the body read (arrayBuffer()) inside the same AbortController deadline as the fetch() call itself, not just the headers — previously the abort only covered the connection/header phase, and a response that started streaming promptly but never finished could still hang past the intended 20s deadline.

tie-permutation.mjs: /llms-full.txt's LAST section is now bounded at the next level-2 '## ' header if one follows it (searched from just past the section's own '### ' line), instead of always running open to end-of-text. Verified live the real file's self-compare is unaffected (its last blog section genuinely runs to true end-of-file, confirmed again this round), and with a synthetic trailing '## Other stuff' section appended, a reorder of the real sections no longer drags that trailing content along with whichever section ends up last.

fixRound2.note: Round 1 (fixRound below, git sha e6518dd) was approved and committed as 4f532b0. This round adds the reviewer's follow-up: extracting and comparing /blog's own embedded post-list data, plus 4 smaller review notes on top of that.

mainItem.gap: /blog and /blog?page=N (BlogPostClient) fetch nothing server-side — the server embeds the FULL post list as a Next.js RSC ('flight') prop and the browser renders/paginates it in JS. Verified live: 0 of 172 post titles land in /blog's extracted visible text and 0 /blog/<slug> links are found (extractHtml strips <script> content before hashing visible text, and the embedded data is never HTML markup). So the listing's titles, excerpts, rendered dates, order and count were entirely invisible to parity — a stale cached /blog or a Vercel date-rendering difference would have passed unnoticed.
fix: lib/extract.mjs: new extractEmbeddedBlogPosts(rawHtml). Every `self.__next_f.push([<n>,"<data>"])` call's <data> is exactly a JSON string literal (JSON.parse('"<data>"') recovers it byte-for-byte, verified against the live site including a doubly-escaped ld+json script's innerHTML); each recovered `<segmentId>:<value>` is parsed as JSON where possible (some are non-JSON 'I[...]' import directives — skipped, not an error), then recursively searched for an array of plain objects that ALL carry a string `slug` field (the shape of the embedded post list, found live at initialPosts — a prop name deliberately not hardcoded). ALWAYS THROWS (never returns []) when it can't find exactly one qualifying array — verified live: /blog and /blog?page=2 both yield exactly 172 posts in the SAME order as /api/blog, with fields {id, title, category, date, slug, author, excerpt, published} (a trimmed subset of /api/blog's own fields — NOT identical, confirmed live); the home page ('/') correctly throws (no such array embedded there at all, since its 4 posts are real server-rendered links, not client-hydrated).

capture.mjs: EMBEDDED_POST_LIST_URL_RE scopes this to exactly '/blog' and '/blog?page=<N>' (never any other page — verified live that no other page embeds a qualifying array, so this can't misfire). Full mode records embeddedPostsSlugOrder (ordered, duplicates preserved) + embeddedPostsBySlug (slug -> canonical JSON, 'every field exact'); compact mode records embeddedPostsSlugOrder + embeddedPostsBySlugHash (slug -> sha256), mirroring buildCompactBlogArrayFields's shape for /api/blog. A parse failure sets its OWN embeddedPostsError field (never silently omits the fields as if the page had zero posts) without discarding the rest of `record.html` that DID extract successfully.

compare.mjs: new comparison block (inside the existing is2xxHtml guard) — per-slug hash equality (every field exact, mode-agnostic via the same on-the-fly-hash-a-full-side pattern as /api/blog) PLUS a strict order-array equality check (embeddedPosts.<order>), both as ordinary FAILING fields. Unlike /api/blog's deliberately order-insensitive compare, a pure reorder here fails by default — a legitimate tie permutation can only be reconciled via an allowlist entry backed by a tie-permutation.mjs proof (A1 C8), never silently accepted. An asymmetric embeddedPostsError between sides is its own comparable field.

tie-permutation.mjs: the 'blog-embedded-json' kind (used for /blog) now calls lib/extract.mjs's extractEmbeddedBlogPosts() directly for BOTH the order check and the residual check (checkBlogPageResidual, now taking {postsA, postsB, slugOrder} — the page's own parsed objects — instead of the old {perSlugHashA, perSlugHashB} sourced from /api/blog). This is the exact fix the reviewer asked for: 'make tie-permutation's /blog residual use the page's own embedded objects instead of /api/blog.'
verifiedLive: extractEmbeddedBlogPosts on /blog and /blog?page=2 each yield exactly 172 posts in identical order to /api/blog and to each other.

capture({compact:false}) and capture({compact:true}) both scoped correctly: embeddedPostsSlugOrder/By Slug(Hash) present ONLY for /blog and /blog?page=2 among 3 test URLs ('/', '/blog', '/blog?page=2'); '/' has neither field nor an error (correctly not attempted).
checkBlogPageResidual with a mutated excerpt correctly fails with reason per-slug-content-mismatch.

Full self-test (see selfTestRun below): all 4 required embedded-post-list mutations (excerpt edited, date changed, missing post, extra post) detected in FULL mode, COMPACT mode, and BOTH mixed-mode directions (8/8 mixed sub-cases); A-vs-A (self-compare-zero-diffs, determinism-two-captures-60s-apart, determinism-compact-mode, mixed-mode-compare-both-directions) all still 0 unexplained diffs with the new fields present.

smallNotesFixed: tie-permutation.mjs: findHrefMatches ('/') and findLlmsLineMatches ('/llms.txt') now bound each post's block to its own card (its closing ) or line (through the trailing newline) instead of leaving it open-ended to the next match/end-of-text — verified live that a reorder's reconstruction no longer drags the page's tail (a 'View all articles' CTA + footer on '/', anything after the last bullet on /llms.txt) along with whichever post ends up last. /sitemap.xml (explicit ... bounds) and /llms-full.txt (the file's last blog section already runs to true end-of-file, confirmed live — no real tail exists there) needed no change.

compare.mjs: readRawText()/readRawTextPlainBody() now VERIFY sha256Text(normalizeText(raw)) (or the .text.txt content's hash) against the manifest's own stored hash (d.a/d.b) before trusting the rawDir file; on a mismatch they report {verified:false, mismatch:true} and the diff gets rawVerificationFailedA/B:true, falling back to the short preview instead of building a unified diff from unverified (possibly stale/from-a-different-run) content. Verified live: corrupting a compact side's raw .bin file without updating its stored hash correctly sets rawVerificationFailedB:true and falls back to preview.

selftest.mjs: new 'tie-swap-real-data' check — finds a REAL pair of posts sharing the exact same created_at in A's own live /llms.txt order (excluding the pinned-fallback slot), swaps them via tie-permutation.mjs's own extractOrderedSlugs/buildReorderedText (new exported utilities, the exact machinery the real residual check itself uses — never a synthetic string), and confirms the swap alone PASSES while the same swap plus one extra edit FAILS. Verified live: swapped 'b2b-sales-tips-strategies-distributors' <-> 'integrating-zoho-crm-b2b-ecommerce-guide' (a genuine tie pair); legit swap passed, swap+edit failed with reason residual-content-difference.

functional/run.mjs: checkCacheHit's two fetches now go through fetchWithTimeout() (AbortController, 20s), and the whole function is wrapped in a try/catch returning {pass:false, detail:{error}} on a timeout/abort instead of letting it hang or crash the suite.

fixRound.note: This supersedes the round-1 evidence written earlier in this file (git sha ae42c88c6b7fc79941f2a6909e8615e226896cec). blockingFixed: tie-permutation.mjs rewritten: checkPageTiePermutation(url, kind, rawTextA, rawTextB, createdAtBySlug, topN) extracts each side's OWN /blog/<slug> occurrence order directly from a real captured page body, checks it against ONE createdAt map built from A's /api/blog only, then (for non-/blog kinds) a byte-identical residual reconstruction. The top-N boundary is a RELATIVE test (B's shown set may differ from A's only within the boundary tie group). Handles lib/storage.ts's pinned ARC AI fallback article.
Added self-test cases built from REAL captured data: 'tie-permutation-real-data' (A-vs-A passes, A-vs-(A+edit) fails, for /, /sitemap.xml, /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt and /blog).
nonBlockingFixed: tie-permutation.mjs: fails loudly on published:false; true multiset slug-set comparison; CLI rejects non-numeric --top-n; tieGranularity:'millisecond' noted.
urls.mjs source 1c: bypassSecret sent ONLY to baseB; 1b/1c recorded AFTER all expect-bearing sources.
functional/run.mjs's checkCacheHit also requires status 200 + non-empty body.
compare.mjs (A1 C10): checkBlogApiSize() always emits both sides' bytes/jsonArrayLength; threshold is exactly 3,500,000 bytes.
compare.mjs: readRawTextPlainBody() raw-.bin-through-normalizeText() fallback for a compact 'text' field, for a real unified diff instead of only a preview.
selftest.mjs: 'mixed-mode-mutation-cases' (field change + text edit, both directions) and 'real-compact-capture-path' (the real capture({compact:true}) path exercised once live).

changedFiles.change: Round 3: the RSC flight parser rewritten to join-then-split (joinFlightPushStrings + splitFlightRows, replacing the old one-row-per-push()-call extractFlightSegments), with 'T' text-row byte-length handling and an empty-id ('bare :HL[...]') fix. extractEmbeddedBlogPosts() now requires EXACTLY ONE candidate array (throws on >1). (Round 2's collectSlugArrays/extractQuotedJsStringAt helpers are otherwise unchanged.)

Round 3: EMBEDDED_POST_LIST_URL_RE now exported (reused by compare.mjs's checkEmbeddedPostsCoverage). capture()'s returned manifest now carries a `harness: {embeddedPosts: 1}` marker. (Round 2's buildFullEmbeddedPostsFields/buildCompactEmbeddedPostsFields and captureOne wiring are otherwise unchanged.)

BLOCKING fix (round 3): the embeddedPostsError diff now fires whenever EITHER side has an error, unconditionally — no longer gated on the two errors differing. New checkEmbeddedPostsCoverage() fails a 2xx /blog(-like) entry with neither embeddedPosts* fields nor an error, gated on the manifest's new harness.embeddedPosts marker. 'embeddedPostsError' and 'embeddedPostsMissing' both added to FORBIDDEN_ALLOWLIST_FIELDS. Imports EMBEDDED_POST_LIST_URL_RE from capture.mjs. (Round 2's per-slug/order comparison and the raw-dir hash-verification fallback are otherwise unchanged.)

Round 3: findLlmsSectionMatches's last section is now bounded at the next level-2 '## ' header if one follows it, instead of always open to end-of-text. (Round 2's blog-embedded-json branch, checkBlogPageResidual signature, and card/line bounding for '/'/'/llms.txt' are otherwise unchanged.)

Round 3: new 'embedded-posts-coverage-guard' check (same-error-both-sides must fail; new-code missing-both must fail; old-manifest missing-both must NOT fail) and new 'flight-row-batching-robustness' check (a real 172-post row merged into one push() call, and split across two, both still extract all 172). (Round 2's embeddedPosts mutation cases, tie-swap-real-data and real-compact-capture-path are otherwise unchanged.)

Round 3: fetchWithTimeout() now wraps the body read (arrayBuffer()) inside the same timeout deadline as the fetch() call, returning {res, body} — not just the headers/connection phase. (Round 2's 20s timeout + try/catch wrapping is otherwise unchanged.)
Unchanged since round 1 (no finding against it in any round) — hash identical.

notScopedAsBulky.note: SPEC-04 addendum item 2 says 'other bulky fields (text, html) should become hashes as well'. Interpreted as: record.text (text/plain bodies, e.g. llms-full.txt) and /api/blog's whole-array/per-slug JSON, PLUS (as of this round) /blog's embedded post-list JSON. HTML pages otherwise never store raw HTML or the extracted visibleText in the manifest (only visibleTextHash, plus moderate-size field/link/asset arrays) in EITHER mode.
